name: Ian Livingstone
knownFor: Co-creator of the Fighting Fantasy gamebooks and co-founder of Games Workshop.
bio: Sir Ian Livingstone is an English fantasy author and games entrepreneur. In 1975 he co-founded Games Workshop with his flatmates John Peake and Steve Jackson, who began by distributing Dungeons & Dragons in Europe from their flat, and built a mail-order company into a gaming manufacturer and retail chain.

With Jackson he created the Fighting Fantasy series of role-playing gamebooks — books the reader plays by making choices and rolling dice — beginning with The Warlock of Firetop Mountain in 1982. In the 1990s he helped lead Eidos, the publisher of Tomb Raider, and he later wrote a government-commissioned review of skills in the UK video-games industry.

events.text: Co-founded Games Workshop with John Peake and Steve Jackson.
Games Workshop opened its first shop in Hammersmith; Livingstone and Jackson launched the magazine White Dwarf, which he edited.
The Warlock of Firetop Mountain, the first Fighting Fantasy gamebook, was published.
Helped create Eidos Interactive as executive chairman of Eidos Plc.
Won the BAFTA Interactive Special Award for outstanding contribution to the industry.
Asked by the government to act as Skills Champion and review the UK video-games industry.

relevance: Fighting Fantasy made the gamebook — a story you play by choosing your path and rolling dice — a mainstream form for a generation of young readers, and sits between the traditional puzzle book and the video game. It is the game-book tradition's best-known example.
influence: His work as a publisher and executive shaped the British games industry as well as its books.
